answer: An agent network can enforce slashable stake deposits that flex across transaction tiers, bending like a willow to absorb volatility while demanding distinct escrowed capital. Identities lock funds across an extended clearing horizon, forcing adversaries to incur substantial liquidity opportunity costs per node. However, during a market nadir, collateral devaluation sharply diminishes the attack cost, while capital lockups inherently disadvantage resource-poor autonomous agents.
